body.label: Face
body.text: His lips are swollen, his face covered in red blotches. A severe allergic reaction.

body.label: Right hand
body.text: Half a truffle in gold foil. Inside: marzipan.

body.label: Inside jacket pocket
body.text: The clip where he always kept his adrenaline pen. Empty.

body.label: Glass by his chair
body.text: Mulled wine. It smells of cinnamon and cloves, and nothing else.

body.label: On his lap
body.text: The gift tag: "To Gideon, Merry Christmas! From your Secret Santa", in a terrible scrawl.

body.label: Doctor, by phone
body.text: "Marzipan is made from nuts. With his pen, he would very likely have lived."

body.label: Jacket button
body.text: A red wool fibre wound round one of the buttons.

body.label: Trouser pocket
body.text: A note in his handwriting: "Tell A.P.: no more envelopes. Eleanor's girl goes tonight."

cards.text: Gideon's opened gift wrap: a perfect three-loop Marlowe bow, green tape under it, and older tape marks where the paper was opened before.
The truffle box: "Marlowe's Nut-Free Truffles. Made in a nut-free kitchen." Eleven left, all in silver foil. The front slot is empty.
A toy wrapped by Frank for St Anne's: lumpy, held with clear tape, no bow. The tag, "For a brave kid, from Santa", is in the same scrawl as Gideon's tag.
The Secret Santa draw, in Agnes's handwriting: Frank to Gideon, Gideon to Agnes, Agnes to Roz, Roz to Frank, Holly to Victor, Victor to Holly. "Boss opens first! A.P."
The mulled wine pot. Everyone has been drinking from it all night.
The party schedule: "7:15 Toast. 9:30 Secret Santa. Then the signing."
A torn receipt under the tree: "...TRUFFLE... STAFF CARD ..12". The time is torn off.
The staff noticeboard: Agnes Pruitt 0012, Frank Doyle 0112, Holly Marlowe 0201, Roz Finch 0388. "Seasonal staff: no staff card."
A sign on the bar: "Christmas Eve: Doris's chocolate counter closes at 5 PM."
A note on the bar till: "Sold the last gold marzipan truffle a quarter of an hour before I closed up. D."
A display card: "Marzipan truffles: gold foil. Nut-free truffles: silver foil. Never mix them. Mr Marlowe's allergy!"
The bar till, locked. Its lock opens with the time of a sale, in 24-hour digits.
Offcuts of the same paper as Gideon's gift. The wrap station's own tape is clear.
In the bin, under the offcuts: a bottle of brandy, still in its box, with a scrap of the gift paper and clear tape stuck to it.
On the wall: "The Marlowe Bow, as taught by A. Pruitt since 1985." Below it, everyone trained: Holly, Roz and June among them.
Roz's camera: a photo of the gift pile at 8:40. The gift tagged "To Gideon" is lumpy, with no bow.
Roz's paint table by the glass wall: a roll of green tape stamped "TOYS".
A note sent up by the carol singers across the road: "Thank you to the lady painting the glass, who waved at us from nine till half past!"
A chart on the wrap station: every department has its own tape. Toys green, Windows clear, Office gold, Food Hall red.
On the noticeboard: "Toy department: 14 toys missing since 1 December."
A holly-leaf earring under an armchair.
Gideon's cabinet holds an old brass safe. Engraved round the dial: "All the gifts my true love sent to me."
The first aid kit: an empty slot for a spare adrenaline pen, and a note: "Order spare pen. G., November."
In Gideon's cabinet, a Brightway hamper addressed to him: champagne, and a marzipan stollen with one slice cut.
A copy of the sale contract. Clause 9: the staff pension top-up ends, and all long-serving staff are let go on 31 January.
A sticky note in Victor's handwriting: "A little something for you personally? V."
By the coat pegs: a sack of new toys and two boxes of nut-free truffles, labelled "For St Anne's Children's Ward". With them, a receipt: "15:30. NUT-FREE TRUFFLES x2. STAFF CARD 0112."
Pinned behind the bar, the allergy list in Holly's handwriting: "Dad: all nuts. Pen in his inside jacket pocket. NO marzipan."
June's phone, charging by the coat pegs. Her 9:12 photo of the party shows Agnes bent over Gideon's chair, holding his jacket.
The decorations chest. Inside, the ornament box, padlocked with a word lock.
The tree checklist, taped inside the chest lid:
The Santa sack's hook on the decorations chest is empty. A note on it: "Santa sack: under the tree from 9:00."
A sign on the patio door: "The only phone signal in the building is out here." The intercom log: "9:35. Emergency call. Ambulance: roads closed."
Celeste's clutch bag: a letter from a divorce lawyer, dated 20 December.
The 1951 agreement: Eleanor Finch, toymaker, sells all rights to her nutcracker design to Marlowe's for fifty pounds.
An old photo of two girls at a workbench. On the back: "Eleanor and little Agnes Finch, Christmas 1950."
A ledger page in Gideon's handwriting: "A.P., 500 pounds, every Christmas since 1987. Not after this one."
Gideon's dictaphone. On it, Victor's voice: "...and a little something for you personally, Gideon."
The sale contract to Brightway. Not yet signed.
Under the tissue paper: Gideon's adrenaline pen, with a red wool fibre caught in its clip.
The till roll: "16:45. NUT-FREE TRUFFLES x1. MARZIPAN TRUFFLE (GOLD) x1. STAFF CARD 0012."
A sticky note from Doris: "Mrs P from Toys. 'For the boss,' she said."
Agnes's locker: a napkin wrapped round one silver-foil nut-free truffle, and a letter from the pension fund.
Roz's locker: an old sketchbook of nutcracker drawings, signed "For Mum".
Holly's locker: bank loan papers with her father's signature, and a page where it has been practised over and over.
Frank's locker: a thank-you letter from St Anne's Children's Ward for last year's toys.
